I estimated the ATT with inverse propensity weighting. I fit a logistic regression of treatment `t` on x0–x16, then reweighted the control group by the odds ps/(1−ps) to match the treated group. This gives an ATT of about 0.099 on the binary outcome `y`.

The naive difference in means is negative (−0.073): treated 0.782 versus control 0.855. Adjusting for the confounders reverses the sign.

Other adjustment methods give somewhat different values:

| Method | ATT estimate |
|---|---|
| Inverse propensity weighting (reported) | 0.099 |
| Regression adjustment (outcome model fit on controls) | 0.084 |
| OLS with a treatment dummy | 0.081 |

I picked inverse propensity weighting as the standard ATT estimator, but the choice is a judgment call, and the answer depends on it.

ANSWER: 0.099
